Brandenburg is my favorite nation to play focused solely on European conquest (Portugal for colonization and England for a mix of the two) and this is my Brandenburg/Prussia strategy. I've used it at least half dozen times with great success; it works on 1.11 if you're still playing that, and it works even better on 1.12 with Paradox adding a bunch of new provinces to the Baltic area strengthening Brandenburg's position. I haven't tested it on 1.13, but it should work fine with that too. The only caveat being that with the change of AI allies only joining one offensive war every 10 years, you'll have to juggle your allies a bit and not call them into every war. After your first few wars, allies go from "necessary" to "helpful" unless you're fighting France or the Ottomans, so this shouldn't be too big a deal.

If you want to be colonial power, then this guide isn't for you.
If you want to go tall rather than wide, then this guide isn't for you.
If you want to become emperor and do the HRE thing, then this guide isn't for you.
If you want to stick to historical Prussia, then this guide isn't for you.
If you want to focus on becoming Germany, then this guide isn't for you.

This is a guide on how to create a wide Baltic & Northern German Empire as Brandenburg/Prussia.

Opening Moves:

Check to make sure all of the following are true:
1. Saxe-Lauenburg has a green heart towards you
2. Denmark and Poland haven't rivaled each other, neither one way nor mutual
3. Austria has rivaled Bohemia

If any of these aren't the case, then restart. Rival the following: Mecklenburg, Bohemia, and the Teutonic Order. Switch your HRE vote from yourself to Austria; +25 same religion, +25 they voted for us, and same rival bonus for rivaling Bohemia should allow you to immediately royal marriage Austria and then ally them. Use your other diplomat to royal marriage and ally Denmark and Poland. Look at the OPMs to the west of you, particularly Saxe-Lauenburg, Lüneburg, Magdeburg, and Anhalt, and RM + ally any who have a green heart towards you. Saxe-Lauenburg is the vitally important one as that prevents the Hansa from connecting their territory and allows Denmark to march troops into your own territory to help in wars. Go over the relationship limit if you have to, you'll want to vassalize all the ones who are friendly towards you as soon as possible and allying them shields them from the aggressive expansion you're about to take.

This may take a couple of attempts to get right, but you should have RMs + alliances with Austria, Poland, Denmark, Saxe-Lauenburg, and one or two other OPMs to your west within the first 4 or 5 months of the game. Focus on getting Austria, Poland, and Denmark first before the -20 too many diplomatic relationships modifier kicks in.

Initial war:

Keep an eye on Poland, you want to have all your diplomacy setup and go to war BEFORE they get the PU over Lithuania. One of the conditions for the PU to fire is that Poland has to be at peace, so if you can get Poland into a war before they get the PU and keep them there for a few years until Poland gets it's own king, then the PU will never fire. Yes, this will make Poland a weaker ally in the short-term, but that's much better than having to deal with a combined Poland-Lithuania in a century or two. If Poland gets the PU before you finish your diplomacy and are ready for war, restart the game.

Take the mission to reconquer your core of Neumark currently owned by the Teutonic Order. The Teutonic Order should be allied to Mecklenburg, the Livonian Order, and Hungary. Declare war on TO for Neumark. Austria and Poland should definitely be willing to join you; Denmark may not be, but they're not essential. Let Austria and Poland deal with Hungary and TO while you siege Mecklenburg. Annex Mecklenburg once that's done and start coring immediately, congrats you now have a coast. Next, move on to knocking Hungary out of the war, just force them to cancel their alliance with TO and give you some money and war reps, you don't want to weaken them as that gives the Ottomans an easier time expanding into Europe. Now focus on the TO. They have a lot of forts, so this could take awhile.

Poland should have the mission "Conquer Western Prussia" which gives it claims on the four provinces of Danzig, Tuchel, Kulm, and Marienburg, you're not going to be giving Poland any land so try to be the one to occupy these provinces yourself so that you don't get the -100 didn't give us claims or cores in peace deal relations hit. If you can't, it's not a huge deal since +25 same religion, +25 RM, +50 alliance should allow you to keep your Polish ally regardless. The only TO province you absolutely must occupy yourself is Memel. If Poland gets that occupation instead, restart the game.

White peace the Livonian Order, don't take anything from them (not even money), you want the truce to be as short as possible. Take Neumark and Memel, humiliate, and take money and war reps from TO; take as much as you can without taking more land, you want this truce to be as long as possible. You already have a core in Neumark and you should be able to core Memel as soon as Mecklenburg's Wismar and Rostock finish coring.

Second war:

Since you eliminated Mecklenburg, you'll need to pick a new rival. Pick the Livonian Order if possible, if not Pomerania is fine. Once Memel is cored, fabricate a claim on Goldingen, the Livonian province north of Memel. Spend the 5 year truce timer with the Livonian Order letting your manpower recover, paying off any loans, building trade ships, and vassalizing your OPM allies.

As soon as your truce with the Livonian Order is over, you'll want to be at war with them, but you don't necessarily need to declare on them directly. The LO should be allied with some combination of the Hansa, TO, Riga, Lithuania, and Novgorod. If their allies are weak, attack LP directly, if not attack one of their allies and drag them into the war. For example, if they're allied to both the Hansa and Lithuania and you don't want to fight Lithuania yet, then fabricate on the Hansa and attack them instead, LO will have to defend them. In fact, it might be better that way, so that you don't have to worry about grabbing those 4 TO provinces before Poland can get them again (although that should be easier this time, since you won't be busy with Mecklenburg). If TO is in the war, take Ortelsburg, humiliate, and money and war reps; remember nothing to Poland and long truce timers with TO.

Your primary goal in the war is to get Goldingen, Reval, and Narwa from the LO. Once the war is over, core them and start fabricating claims on Ingermanland and Neva.

By this time Denmark should have taken Ösel, so you should be able to march your troops from Berlin, through Poland (get military access), Ortelsburg, Memel, Goldingen, Ösel (get military access), Reval, and all the way to Narwa to deal with any rebel trouble.

Back to the West:

By this time the AE you took from annexing Mecklenburg should have burned off, so while your eastern AE has time to go down, your LO provinces are coring, and you're fabricating claims on Novgorod, it's time to do some more expanding in the HRE.

There are three options here, the best one will be based on how your game is unfolding:
1) attack and annex the OPMs which were hostile to you at the beginning of the game
2) attack Bohemia, take their two Saxon culture provinces and force them to release Silesia
3) take the Pomeranian succession mission and eat some of Pomerania

You'll want to do all of these eventually, so there's really no wrong answer, just watch your AE and avoid coalitions.

Smashing Novgorod:

You should have been able to do all this quickly enough that Muscovy hasn't had time to deal with Novgorod yet. Novgorod usually doesn't have any allies; so use your claims on Ingermanland and Neva to declare war on them, Denmark should be happy to help you. Take Ingermanland, Neva, and Novgorod in the peace deal. This is extremely important. Without Ingermanland and Neva, Muscovy can't build a navy, and without Novgorod, Muscovy can't form Russia. Since Moscovy can't form Russia, they don't get the automatic claims in the Russia and Steppes regions, which makes them less aggressive and easier to handle. Also, Neva and Novgorod have trade modifiers giving you some nice trade power in the Novgorod trade node.

The rest is up to you:

Congrats, you're now setup to completely dominate the southern Baltic in short order. You'll have an increasingly good presence in the Lübeck, Baltic Sea, and Novgorod nodes for income, you have very good strong allies, and the two sides of your country are far enough apart that aggressive expansion from one end won't effect the other.

Your strategy from here on out will be to oscillate between fighting in the HRE and fighting in eastern Europe. Eat some of Lithuania, then go attack the Hansa; chip away at Muscovy, then annex half of Saxony; rinse and repeat, etc. etc. Just always keep an eye on your AE.

General notes on some important countries:

Austria: It is in your best interests to keep Austria as the emperor. They won't join your internal HRE wars, but they also won't demand unlawful territory either. Just keep an eye on imperial reforms and if they're getting close to Ewiger Landfriede (no internal HRE wars), then switch your vote to someone else and force a drop in imperial authority with a transfer of the emperor title. Other AI countries aren't nearly as good at building imperial authority as Austria is, so you'll be able to switch your vote back to Austria and get them as emperor again after a few reforms get revoked or the Reformation fires and the imperial authority modifier goes deep red.

Denmark: Denmark is a great ally early on, especially in the first couple wars against Novgorod/Muscovy. However you do NOT want them annexing Sweden and forming Scandinavia. So keep an eye on them and their other allies, and when the time is right, drop your alliance with them and support Swedish independence. Once Sweden is free, they become your new northern ally and you should start eating Ösel, Bornholm, and the Jutland peninsula. Try to take as much Danish land as possible before Sweden can (don't call Sweden into your anti-Danish wars if you don't need them), but be aware that taking Danish territory that Sweden has cores, not claims, on will cause them to end your alliance with them; i.e. Gotland and the Scanian provinces.

Poland: Poland will love you and be willing to join just about every war you fight, so it is very important to keep them happy. Unfortunately you have the issue of the Teutonic Order's provinces standing between you. Those are YOUR provinces, why should Poland be allowed to take them? So whenever you go to war with TO, be sure that you're the one who occupies the TO provinces Poland has claims on to avoid taking the -100 relation hit for didn't give us claims or cores in peace deal modifier. You can take one of those hits and still maintain your alliance, but generally not two and that modifier decays very slowly (-1 per year).

Check to see which mission Poland has and KNOW WHAT IT MEANS:
"Conquer Western Prussia": gives claims on the four provinces of Danzig, Tuchel, Kulm, and Marienburg, don't take any of those and you're fine.
"Recover Danzig": gives a claim on Danzig, don't take Danzig and you're fine.
"Remind the Knights of their duty": gives a vassalization CB, as long as you don't annex or vassalize TO then you're fine.

Note that these mission do expire. Generally Poland will take "Conquer Western Prussia" first, but will lose it after awhile (50 or 60 years, I think?) and then take one of the other two instead. After that happens you are free to take Tuchel, Kulm, and Marienburg without any problems. Taking territory required by Poland for their mission WILL result in them immediately hating you and cancelling your alliance, and usually rivaling and attacking you soon as well.

Make sure that you're the war leader whenever you go to war with the TO. Take one or two provinces not required for the Polish mission, humiliate if possible, take all their money, ask for war reps, cancel alliances, revoke cores, and anything else to make the war score as high as possible and the truce as long as possible. As soon as the truce is over, declare war on the TO again before Poland can, rinse and repeat. Doing this should allow you to slowly eat the TO while keeping Poland happy for decades.

No matter what you do, Poland will hate you when you inevitably have to take Danzig as the last TO province, so be aware of that and have a plan to backstab them in place and ready to go. Forcing Poland to spit out Mazovia, diplo-vassaling Mazovia, and then feeding Poland's land to your new vassal is a good strategy.

Bohemia: Bohemia starts the game with two Saxon culture provinces and as overlord of Silesia. Saxon is your primary culture and you don't want them diplo-annexing Silesia, so attacking Bohemia should be near the top of your HRE to do list. Take the Saxon provinces and force them to end their vassalization of Silesia. If you ally + RM Silesia then you should be able to vassalize and diplo-annex them yourself. Bohemian provinces are very expensive to core, so only eat away at Bohemia's Czech provinces until you can forcibly vassalize them and then diplo-annex the rest. Avoid trying to core Praha if at all possible, it's usually insanely expensive.

Rest of the German HRE: Use a combination of diplo-annexation and military conquest to expand west and south into the HRE. Ideally you should always have between 5 and 20 AE and 25+ annexed a member of the HRE modifiers at all times; more than that and you have diplomatic problems and get coalitions, less than that and you aren't expanding fast enough.

Use the +100 released in peace relations modifier to maximum effect. Let neighboring OPMs get annexed, then go to war, free them, vassalize them, and diplo-annex them yourself.

Keep in mind:
+100 released in peace
+50 alliance
+25 royal marriage
+10 guarantee
+10 military access
+varies transfer trade power
+25 gift

-any religious, rival, AE, or annexation modifiers

You only need +190 to vassalize someone, so it's very possible to hit that with a released in peace country without even having to improve relations with them.

This strategy works especially well if you're using a mod like the European Province 'Fix' 1.12 mod, which I personally love, that adds a lot of new provinces and revolt shields.

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=451040975

Example: in one of my Brandenburg games, I ended up annexing three different Brunswicks. Brunswick expanded to five provinces and cored them all, then they got dog-piled and Mainz took two of their provinces and Münster took two more, reducing Brunswick to a OPM. I attacked and militarily annexed the OPM Brunswick. I then attacked Münster and forced them to release Brunswick from the two cores they had and used the +100 released in peace modifier to quickly vassalize them and then diplo-annexed that Brunswick 10 years later. And finally I attacked and force Mainz to release Brunswick from the two cores they held as well and did the same thing. So I got Brunswick's five provinces while only getting hit for the AE of one.

Muscovy: If you followed my guide, then you should have been able to prevent Muscovy from forming Russia and getting a Baltic Sea port. This puts Muscovy in a weaker position, but doesn't eliminate it as a threat. Watch Muscovy closely, when they get into wars with their Muslim horde neighbors wait until their manpower gets low and then attack them. Take their provinces and/or force them to release vassals and split out previously annexed countries. Forcing them to release Perm should be your #1 priority in your first war with Muscovy so that they can't start colonizing Siberia. Your goal should be to keep Muscovy permanently weak and off balance.

Lithuania: Lithuania can seem a little bit daunting to take on, but remember that you have stronger allies and that they're eastern tech and you're western tech. Your military and tech superiority is just going to grow over time. Also keep in mind that Lithuania has cores for a number of non-existent countries like Galicia-Volhynia and Smolensk, and forcing it to release some of them can really help weaken them for future wars. Jumping on opportunities like Lithuania fighting Muscovy or Crimea is a very good idea.

Hungary: Hungary would make a great ally, except for the fact that Austria and Poland are generally mutually rivaled with them. Once you backstab Poland or if you can't maintain your alliance with Austria for some reason, look at Hungary as a replacement ally. They can be very helpful against the Ottomans later on.

England/Great Britain: You and England really don't have any conflicting interests. You may occasionally end up at war with them if they ally German minors, but you can generally just dock up your fleet, ignore them, and finish the war before they become a problem. Try to keep your relations high with them as you may need their help against France eventually.

France: France isn't generally an immediate threat, but keep an eye on them after the first century or so and if they're expanding into the HRE look for allies in England and/or Spain to help you and Austria counter that.

Ottomans: Unless Hungary just completely collapses, then you shouldn't have to worry about the Ottomans for the first couple centuries. But keep an eye on the Balkans and if they're expanding too aggressively into Europe, then you'll probably want to deal with them in some way, preferably earlier than later. Be aware that Crimea and the Ottomans are usually allied, so when you eat through Lithuania all the way to the Black Sea that's going to create a conflict with them via their Crimean proxy.

Castile/Spain: Spain is far enough away that you really shouldn't have any interaction with them, especially for the first couple centuries. But if you're running up against France and Spain is their rival, then trying to get an alliance with them is a good idea to help you against the BBB.

Ideas:

Your first idea group should be either Diplomatic or Influence, your second idea group should be Quantity, and your third idea group should be either Religious or Humanist.

You need either Influence or Diplomatic for more dip reputation and dip relations plus either an extra diplomat or lowered AE, after you take the first two Quantity ideas then you should never have manpower problems ever again, and you'll need either Humanist or Religious to handle the religious turmoil of the Reformation.

You also need to use your first and third idea combinations to deal with your cultural problems. You're going to have Russians, Saxons, Danes, Poles, Latvians, and Czechs all inside the same country and that will cause issues. There are two ways of handling that, either lower your accepted culture threshold or culture conversion. If you're going to go with Religious as your third idea, then Influence should be your first one; if you're going to go with Humanist as your third idea, then Diplomatic should be your first one.

Full Religious: -25% culture conversion cost
Religious + Influence policy: -20% culture conversion cost

Fourth Humanist idea: -50% accepted culture threshold
Humanist + Diplomatic policy: -10% accepted culture threshold

For the rest of your idea groups, I recommend, in no particular order:
ADM: Economic
DIP: Trade, Maritime, and Influence/Diplomatic (whichever one you didn't pick as your first group)
MIL: Offensive, Quality

Which ones you pick and in what order will be based on your personal tastes and the needs of the situation you're facing at the time.

Religion:

You will either need to go Protestant or Reformed in order to form Prussia, which you will want to do. I would recommend Protestant as the new church power mechanic is very powerful if you own the Common Sense DLC; go Reformed if you don't.

The religious turmoil will slow down your expansion while you're converting and putting down rebels, but you should be rich enough to spend 500 ducats for the defender of the faith title and get that extra missionary. A Center of Reformation in your country plus two missionaries should allow you to get your religious unity up fairly quickly.

If you've been doing a good job of improving relations with your allies, you should be able to keep all of them even if they stay Catholic. How you want to play the League War or just stay out of it entirely is up to you.

I choose −5% idea cost, +2.5% discipline, and +10% manpower recovery speed as the three aspects of faith for the Church of Prussia; +5% morale of armies or +10% production efficiency are also good choices.

Trade:

Lübeck will be where you collect trade. You will want to use your initial two merchants to transfer trade power from the Baltic Sea and either collect in Lübeck or transfer trade power from Novgorod (check periodically to see which of the last two gets you more money after you conquer Neva and Novgorod).

You should take the Trade idea group as either your 4th, 5th, or 6th idea group which will give you three additional merchants:

  • 1) North Sea to Lübeck
  • 2) Baltic Sea to Lübeck
  • 3) Rhineland to Lübeck
  • 4) Either Saxony to Lübeck OR Wien to Rhineland
  • 5) Either Novgorod to Baltic Sea OR collect in Lübeck

Conclusion:

Well I think that just about covers everything. I hope you found this helpful whether you decide to follow it to the letter or just adopt parts of it. If you have any questions, please ask and I'll do my best to answer them.
